text: The Patriots are dealing with some significant roster shuffling as they prepare for Sunday's 1 PM ET home opener against the Steelers at Gillette Stadium, most notably the loss of wide receiver A.J. Brown, who suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 1 and will miss at least four games after being placed on injured reserve—forcing Mike Vrabel's offense to find new contributors to fill that void. To shore up the defense, the team signed free agent DT DaQuan Jones on a one-year deal worth up to $6 million, while on the practice squad side they've been active, signing WR Chandler Brayboy and LB Xavier Holmes while releasing S Elliott Davison and RB Hassan Haskins after earlier re-signing Davison. Off the field, owner Robert Kraft made headlines by explaining his decision to have rapper Macklemore removed as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's shows at Gillette Stadium, citing his history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that Kraft said has been offensive to the Jewish community. With Brown sidelined and new pieces coming in on both sides of the ball, the question now is how quickly this squad can gel against a tough Steelers defense.
